text.content: This lesson will introduce you to the project. You will work on completing the following policies: memory, conversation, and self-assessment. This validates your understanding of agent memory architecture and your ability to apply it. You will produce a written memory policy, run a multi-turn conversation test against your configured Chatflow, and complete a knowledge quiz. All three tasks are required.

text.content: Sprint 1 has taken you through the full arc of agent memory from understanding why stateless models fail in business conversations, to distinguishing memory from knowledge bases and tools, to configuring Buffer Memory, Session IDs, and Buffer Window Memory, and defining the rules that govern what an agent should and should not store.

text.content: This assessment asks you to bring those pieces together. The scenario is Contigo GmbH's support agent, which you have been building and refining across the sprint. It is now approaching a production readiness review. Before it can be deployed to real clients, the team needs documented evidence that memory has been designed deliberately, not just configured and left to run.
